title: Application Secrets and Configuration Patterns
description: Review common patterns for securely managing secrets and configuration in Azure applications.

data.text: As applications grow, managing configuration becomes harder. Several patterns help keep secrets safe and configuration maintainable across development, staging, and production.

data.title: Patterns to Know
items: Managed Identity + Key Vault — no secrets in code
App Configuration + Key Vault references — centralized settings
Environment variables for local dev — .env files ignored by git
User-assigned managed identity — shared identity across resources
GitHub Secrets + Azure login — CI/CD without long-lived credentials

data.title: Local Development with .env and DefaultAzureCredential
data.content: Use environment variables locally and managed identities in Azure.

data.title: GitHub Actions with Azure Login
data.content: Deploy from GitHub without storing long-lived secrets in your repo.
data.code:
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/login@v1
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}
      - run: az webapp up --name myApp --resource-group myRG

data.caption: How configuration flows from vaults and App Configuration into your app.
data.definition:
flowchart LR
    KV["Key Vault"] -->|"Secret references"| AC["App Configuration"]
    AC -->|"Settings + flags"| App["Application"]
    MI["Managed Identity"] -->|"Authenticates"| KV
    MI -->|"Authenticates"| AC

data.title: Never Commit Secrets
data.text: Always add .env, appsettings.Production.json with real values, and any file containing secrets to .gitignore. Scan your repository with tools like git-secrets or GitHub secret scanning.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: DefaultAzureCredential adapts to local dev, CI, and Azure automatically.
Combine Key Vault, App Configuration, and managed identities for defense in depth.
Never hardcode secrets or store them in source control.
data.takeaway: The best secret is the one you never have to store. Managed identities make that possible.
